beats.label: S1 · Korra runs to Republic City
beats.text: Seventeen-year-old Avatar Korra, master of three elements but unable to airbend, flees her White Lotus compound for Republic City to train under Tenzin, Aang's son.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Korra's core problem — airbending block — and her arrival in the city where every following event happens.

beats.label: S1 · Amon reveals his power
beats.text: At an anti-bender Equalist rally, the masked leader Amon permanently strips gangsters of their bending, a power no one thought possible outside the Avatar.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's antagonist and the threat that reframes every bender's stakes.

beats.label: S1 · The duel that breaks her
beats.text: Korra challenges Amon alone and is captured. He spares her bending to avoid making a martyr, but the encounter leaves her genuinely terrified for the first time in her life.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First crack in Korra's confidence — the psychological weight she carries through the rest of the season.

beats.label: S1 · Hiroshi Sato exposed
beats.text: Industrialist Hiroshi Sato is revealed as the Equalists' weapons supplier, arming them with mecha-tanks. His daughter Asami sides against him and joins Korra's group on Air Temple Island.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns the Equalists from a movement into a military force and locks in the friend group.

beats.label: S1 · Tarrlok's secret
beats.text: Councilman Tarrlok abducts Korra and reveals himself as a bloodbender and the son of the criminal Yakone. Amon soon finds him and takes his bending too.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the family reveal that ends the season and shows Amon turning on his own allies.

beats.label: S1 · Republic City falls
beats.text: Equalist airships bomb the city and capture the council. Lin Beifong is stripped of her bending shielding Tenzin's family; General Iroh's relief fleet is destroyed on arrival.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The city is lost — the state Korra must reverse in the finale, and the scale of Amon's win.

beats.label: S1 · Amon unmasked, Korra restored
beats.text: Korra exposes Amon as Tarrlok's waterbending brother Noatak and airbends for the first time. He strips her other three elements, but Aang's spirit restores her and unlocks the Avatar State.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the season's villain and Korra's airbending block, but leaves her spiritual connection newly opened.

cliffhanger.text: Amon is dead, the Equalist uprising broken, and Korra is a fully realised Avatar for the first time — airbending mastered, bending restored, Aang's spirit having reached her directly. She has her power back, but she has never lived as the Avatar the world expects her to be.
questions: Now that she can contact Aang, what will Korra do with a spiritual connection she has never used?
With Mako choosing Korra over Asami, where does that leave the group's friendships?
Who steps into the power vacuum in Republic City with the council gone and Lin Beifong's force gutted?

characters.name: Korra
characters.line: The seventeen-year-old Avatar from the Southern Water Tribe, headstrong and physical, now able to bend all four elements after Aang restored what Amon took.

characters.name: Tenzin
characters.line: Aang and Katara's son, the only airbending master and Korra's mentor, a councilman and father of four young airbending children.

characters.name: Mako
characters.line: Firebending pro-bender, orphaned older brother to Bolin, ended the season with Korra after breaking things off with Asami.

characters.name: Bolin
characters.line: Earthbending pro-bender and Mako's easygoing younger brother, part of Korra's inner circle.

characters.name: Asami Sato
characters.line: Non-bender heiress and skilled driver who turned on her Equalist father Hiroshi; recently displaced from her home and dumped by Mako.

characters.name: Lin Beifong
characters.line: Toph's daughter and former metalbending police chief, stripped of her bending by Amon while protecting Tenzin's family — bending later restored by Korra.

characters.name: Amon / Noatak
characters.line: The Equalist leader, revealed as Tarrlok's waterbending brother; presumed dead after Tarrlok blew up their escape boat.

characters.name: Hiroshi Sato
characters.line: Asami's father and the industrialist who armed the Equalists with mecha-tanks and airships; defeated and captured in the finale.
